title: Care Home Support Worker - &;23p/h
description:
Residential Support Worker - Scottish Island (£23/hr, 45+ hrs/week)

Are you an experienced Residential Support Worker or Care Assistant looking for your next rewarding, high-paying contract? Take your care expertise to some of the UK's most beautiful, ruggedly scenic coastal destinations. We are fast-tracking applications for 3-month placements within established, welcoming care homes across Shetland, Orkney, and the Western Isles. Combine high earning potential with the unique experience of island living!

Note: We are looking for female staff at the moment due to requirements and demand for the role.

What We Offer
- Competitive Pay: Earn £23.00/hr (Umbrella) with guaranteed 45+ hours per week.
- Adventure & Impact: Experience breathtaking coastal landscapes and close-knit island communities.
- Relocation Support: We welcome candidates from across the UK and provide assistance with travel and placement logistics.
- Quick Start: Benefit from a streamlined hiring process.
- Contract Duration: Minimum 3 months.

Responsibilities
- Provide high-quality, person-centered care, including assistance with dressing, mobility, and personal hygiene in line with individual care plans.
- Safely administer prescribed medications and monitor resident health and overall well-being.
- Utilize safe moving and handling techniques to ensure the comfort and dignity of residents.
- Maintain a secure and supportive living environment, demonstrating the ability to manage tasks effectively, including during periods of lone working.

Qualifications
- Minimum of 1 year of professional care experience supporting older adults (care home experience preferred).
- Demonstrated competency in personal care, medication administration, and safe moving and handling practices.
- Willingness and ability to relocate or travel for a 3-month contract.
- Possession of a driving license is preferred for regional travel, though not mandatory.
- Note: Due to specific resident personal care requirements across select care homes, we have active requirements for female care professionals (Exempt under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1). We also welcome applications from all qualified care professionals for broader regional placements.

Employment Details
- Work Location: Shetland, Orkney, and the Western Isles
- Expected Hours: 45+ hours per week

Don't wait-high-rate island placements fill quickly!

title: Learning Support Assistant
company: The Supply Register Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Learning Support Assistant

Contract: Full-time, Temporary (ongoing)
Employer: The Supply Register, on behalf of Tyne Coast College
Location: South Tyneside College
Salary: £14.91-£16.28 per hour (inclusive of holiday pay)

About the Role

The Supply Register is seeking passionate, dedicated and supportive Learning Support Assistants (LSAs) to join South Tyneside College on a full-time, temporary basis.

This is an excellent opportunity to make a meaningful difference to students by providing tailored support to learners with a range of additional learning needs. As an LSA, you will play an important role in creating an inclusive, positive and supportive learning environment, helping students overcome barriers and achieve their academic, personal and progression goals.

Working closely with teaching staff, you will provide support across classroom, small-group and one-to-one settings, adapting your approach to meet individual learner needs. You will help students develop confidence, independence and essential skills, enabling them to make meaningful progress throughout their learning programme.

If you are passionate about supporting young people and adults, enjoy helping others succeed and are committed to creating an inclusive learning environment, we would love to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide tailored learning support to students in classroom, workshop and practical learning environments.
- Support learners with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), learning difficulties and additional support requirements.
- Work alongside teaching staff to deliver engaging, accessible and inclusive learning activities.
- Encourage students to participate actively in their learning and develop greater independence.
- Monitor learner progress and provide relevant feedback to tutors and support teams.
- Help students develop study skills, organisation and positive classroom engagement.
- Provide encouragement and practical support to help learners build confidence and achieve their goals.
- Assist with personal care needs where required and appropriate.
- Promote safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion throughout the learning environment.
- Work collaboratively with teaching and support teams to ensure learners receive consistent and effective support.

title: Support Worker
description:
Helping others improve and turn their lives around - there's no better feeling. It's what we do for thousands of people at more than 150 sites across the UK. Be a part of it.

We are looking for confident Support Workers with a passion for delivering outstanding care.

You'll be working 42 hours a week in Thornfield Grange with Adults with Learning Disabilities and Autism along with behaviours that challenge.

Working shifts of 7.45am to 8pm and 7.45pm to 8am, inhouse meals are provided and paid handovers. This role involves working every other weekend.

Thornfield Grange is a specialist residential service with nursing for adults with autism, learning disabilities and complex needs. Based in Bishop Auckland, County Durham, Thornfield Grange supports individuals who have behaviours that may challenge, as well as those who have significant difficulties with social engagement.

The role involves supporting adults with all aspects of daily life, including on occasion personal care. Accessing the community regular and taking service users on holidays and driving responsibilities.

Your Day-to-Day
- Offer enhanced care with a flexible learning approach for all our service users, patients & residents
- Provide guidance and encouragement through physical & emotional support
- Learn about individuals' specific needs & provide help in the most appropriate way
- Assist with medical & welfare needs and report as required
- Safeguard
- Maintain a safe and clean environment for all

You are
- Genuinely driven with a desire to make a real difference in people's lives
- An excellent communicator and a good team player
- Sensitive and intuitive with the energy required to provide a trusting, stimulating & varied environment
- Helping to empower & support service user independence

Why Cygnet? We'll offer you
- £13.15 per hour increasing to £13.45 per hour at 3 months and £13.70 per hour at 18 months
- An opening to undertake further learning with our excellent apprenticeship scheme
- Flexible working with opportunity for overtime
- Regular coaching & appraisal
- Expert supervision & peer support
- Employee discount savings & Cycle to Work scheme
- Wellbeing centre with exercises, recipes, financial and mental health advice
- DBS paid
- NHS and blue discount
- 24 hours free GP helpline
- On site benefits including free meals
- Plus much more

Please note: successful candidates will be required to undergo an enhanced DBS check.
